ms.promise: Audit covering whole infrastructure. That includes precompiled contracts, solidity contracts, backend service and provider npm package. Audit also covered invented mechanism of refunding gas for transaction. Remedies to the findings.
ms.criteria: Fixed all of the user facing vulnerabilities
ms.report:
Original:
This is the audit to the wrapped smart contracts by Arbitrary Execution: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k-4_ozGGzxOVlnDFqHkMjzwzgU8M40eK/view?usp=sharing (final version where we fixed all the issues that came up during the audit). The code base is of course open sourced and it can be found here: https://github.com/dcSpark/wrapped-smartcontracts

Comment:
Apologies. After reading your refusal, it became clear that we should had used clearer language. Instead of "... where fixed all the issues that came up during the audit" we should had said instead "... we fixed all the security issues that could affect users' funds". As of today, we are not aware of any vulnerability that can put users' fund at risk (none) and furthermore there is no way to censor users' actions either.
We also address the three (valid) points brought up:
H01: To make sense of this issue, we believe it's helpful to briefly explain how Milkomeda Wrapper smart contracts work. A proxy smart contract is deployed in the EVM that can only take "orders" from a transaction that was signed using a specific Cardano (ed25519) private key. The smart contract deployment is deterministic by the user, so it's safe. This smart contract resembles a wallet that can only be controlled by the user through a Cardano wallet. To improve UX, wrapped smart contracts also allow a batcher (named Oracle) to broadcast transactions for the user. As previously mentioned, the transactions are signed by the user, and the Batcher/Oracle only broadcasts them, taking a very small commission that was added by the user. The user is always able to broadcast a transaction themselves if they prefer.
Coming back to the issue: "[H01] ORACLE TRANSACTION VALIDATION VULNERABLE TO TIME -OF-CHECK TO TIME-OF-
USE RACES". This issue is for the Oracle and the oracle only; users' funds are never at risk in any way. What this issue is about is that the Oracle software (run by us) can have a race condition when broadcasting a transaction a

ms.promise: A TypeScript library designed to simplify interactions with Wrapped Smart Contracts (WSCs). This library allows users to execute smart contracts on sidechains or Layer 2 (L2) networks without leaving their Layer 1 (L1) environment
ms.criteria: To provide developers with a seamless and intuitive way to integrate Wrapped Smart Contracts into their C1 DApps.
ms.report: WSCLib finalized and open sourced https://github.com/dcSpark/wrapped-smartcontracts/tree/main/packages/milkomeda-wsc. This library has been used by multiple projects including TangleSwap, SNEK and Blueshift. the link to the npm package can be found here: https://www.npmjs.com/package/milkomeda-wsc

ms.promise:
A React component library built on top of Milkomeda-WSC Lib. This library offers a recommended form of user experience to allow L1 users to interact with WSCs easily. Thanks to Milkomeda-WSC Lib DApp developers integrations will be seamless. 
.
ms.criteria:
The UI library should offer two explicit solutions for integrating the necessary steps and prompts:
・One where the prompts and actions are seamlessly embedded in the DApp frontend.
・Another where the user is presented with a wallet-like interface that can be opened from the frontend.
ms.report:
This easy to integrate library for the Wrapped Smart Contracts (WSC) can be found here https://github.com/dcSpark/wrapped-smartcontracts/tree/main/packages/milkomeda-wsc-ui and also an easy to use example here: https://github.com/dcSpark/wrapped-smartcontracts/tree/main/packages/milkomeda-wsc-ui-next-example

it was already used in production by the TangleSwap team
